transcript:
Header: 2028-09-14 10:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Aisha (Zenith Head of ML), Tom (Zenith Platform), Priya (Zenith Security)

Summary: Quick sync to understand integration surface and constraints for a pilot. Customer mostly evaluating hosted first, but has strict security and observency needs that may push toward Dedicated or Private later.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE, with me is Liam our SE. How's everyone?
00:12 Aisha: Hi Maya, thanks for organizing. I'm Aisha, head of ML at Zenith. We've got Tom and Priya on who cover infra and security.
00:20 Tom: morning all.
00:23 Priya: hi, thanks.
01:01 Maya: Great, goal for today is to understand your integration constraints — SDKs, orchestration like LangChain/LlamaIndex use, how you want to route through proxies or gateways, and observability needs, and then propose a pilot. Does that align?
01:15 Aisha: Yes, exactly. High level — we want to add summarization and routing assistants in our TMS, and we want to evaluate latency and cost. Prefer to start with hosted to get velocity, but security may require Dedicated or Private eventually.
01:30 Liam: makes sense. Quick question on volume — what are you seeing in tokens per minute and typical latency SLOs?
01:40 Aisha: Right now it's exploratory, so bursts from 50 to 1k reqs/min during peak. For user-facing flows we need p50 < 300ms for short prompts, p95 under 1s ideally.
01:56 Tom: and we have a global footprint, so region routing matters. We use an API gateway in front of our services for auth and rate limiting.
02:10 Maya: good to know. On SDKs: we have official SDKs in JS and Python, plus OpenAPI REST endpoints. We also publish reference LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors — Liam can show the repo after.
02:25 Liam: yeah, the LangChain wrappers are pretty straightforward: chain: LLM -> prompt template -> Redwood client. There are a couple of gotchas we document around streaming + callback handlers. Also LlamaIndex has a small adapter we maintain. Note: occasionally the auto-transcribed name in docs shows "LamaIndex" or "LongChain" — ignore that, it's just the export.
02:48 Priya: on security, our must-haves are SOC2, SSO/SAML with SCIM, audit logs, and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Also we need egress controls — ideally a private endpoint or VPC peering.
03:05 Maya: Redwood supports SOC2, SSO with SAML + SCIM, RBAC, and we do KMS integration. For Private we can offer a VPC private control plane or on-prem bundle. For Dedicated you get dedicated GPU pools and optional VPC. We'll share the security pack after.
03:23 Priya: ok. For audit logs, we need token-level traces for a shortlist of users for compliance, and longer-term aggregated metrics for ops. Are those available?
03:34 Liam: yes — we emit per-request metadata, can stream to your S3, and we support exporting metrics to Prometheus and traces via OpenTelemetry. We also have hooks for structured logs to SIEMs.
03:48 Tom: great. About gateway/proxy: we currently have an Kong-based gateway that enforces quotas and per-tenant ratelimits. We want to keep that in front — can Redwood handle a proxy pattern where our gateway federates calls to Redwood and Redwood also enforces token quotas?
04:06 Maya: yes, common architecture. You can keep the gateway in front. Redwood supports API keys per-route, and you can set per-key quotas on our side too. Many customers use a gateway for initial auth and then pass a short-lived Redwood token. We also have a reverse-proxy example in the SE repo.
04:27 Liam: one note — if you do caching (prefix/KV cache), we recommend providing consistent session keys from the gateway so caching isn't fragmented.
04:40 Aisha: good, we use session-based chat so that matters.
05:02 Tom: about rate limits — what's default for hosted? And can we do bursts for traffic spikes?
05:10 Maya: default hosted quotas are fairly permissive for trial orgs but production you'd pick a plan. Dedicated gives you reserved throughput with burst capacity options. For hosted, we have tiered quotas and can apply dynamic rate limits. We'll include numbers in the pricing packet.
05:27 Liam: also, for predictable latency you can reserve Dedicated capacity — that avoids noisy neighbors and gives predictable p95 latency.
05:40 Aisha: curious about cost per token and also cost per concurrency if we use batching and KV cache.
05:48 Maya: we'll send a cost model spreadsheet. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization profiles to reduce unit costs — we'll show an example for your prompt mix.
06:00 Priya: can we run a pilot in our region? EU data residency is important for a subset of users.
06:08 Liam: yes — we have region-aware routing. For hosted we can pin to EU region endpoints; for Dedicated/Private you can deploy in a customer region. We'll note EEA compliance options in the docs.
06:24 Aisha: integration wise, we plan to use LangChain for retrieval-augmented generation, with LlamaIndex on some ingestion pipelines. Do you have examples for combining both or a recommended pattern?
06:36 Liam: recommended pattern: use LlamaIndex for document store ingestion and indexes, then expose a retrieval interface that LangChain's retriever can call. We have a sample repo with an example using our streaming responses and the LangChain callbacks for token-level logging. We also include best practices for chunking and embedding calls.
06:53 Tom: embeddings — do we call Redwood embeddings or do our own? We currently use a local embedding service (Faiss + inhouse).
07:03 Maya: you can do either. Many customers use Redwood embeddings for simplicity; others keep embeddings in-house and call Redwood only for the LLM. If you keep embeddings local, fine — just ensure the retriever returns passages and you call Redwood for generation.
07:20 Aisha: latency-sensitive flows might prefer on-prem embeddings to avoid extra hops.
07:26 Liam: yes, and we can co-locate inference via Dedicated/private to reduce cross-network latency.
07:40 Priya: about observability hooks, specifically: metrics, traces, and raw transcripts for a short retention window. How granular are these and can we redact PII before it leaves our VPC?
07:54 Liam: we can standardize redaction at the SDK or gateway layer; we also support server-side redaction rules for certain fields. Metrics and traces can be exported to your Prometheus/OpenTelemetry backends. Raw transcript exports can be to your S3 with lifecycle rules — you control retention and encryption.
08:14 Priya: do you integrate with KMS providers like AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / HashiCorp?
08:21 Maya: yes, we integrate with AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault and also support bringing your own HSM via our Private offering.
08:30 Aisha: one question on model fallbacks. If our preferred model is down or capacity is constrained, can Redwood automatically fallback to a compatible variant without changing our API?
08:43 Liam: yes — smart routing supports fallbacks to compatible models in the same family with automatic prompt rewriting if necessary. You can configure routing policies per-route: latency-first, cost-first, or failover.
08:58 Tom: any incompatibilities with LlamaIndex if you do quantized models or special kernels?
09:07 Liam: generally no, but edge cases exist if you use extreme quantization for retrieval-augmented workflows. We document model/quantization matrices and recommended kernels in the model catalog. We also provide performance profiles per model.
09:24 Aisha: okay — what's the recommended approach for a short pilot? Hosted or Dedicated?
09:31 Maya: recommended: hosted for fastest time-to-value — you can validate prompts and UX quickly. If you need strict data residency or customer-managed keys we recommend Dedicated or Private for the pilot. Given your security ask, a dedicated pilot with VPC peering might be a good compromise.
09:47 Priya: we prefer to start hosted but only if the hosted isolation and KMS options meet our bar. Otherwise we want a short dedicated pilot.
09:58 Maya: understood — we'll include both options in the pricing pack.
10:08 Liam: a quick note about integration: we can provide a small SDK patch to run behind your gateway that issues short-lived tokens to Redwood and adds session keys for caching. That prevents exposing long-lived keys in the frontend.
10:22 Tom: yes we want that pattern. Also — do you support per-tenant quotas inside a single org? We have multi-tenant customers on our platform.
10:34 Liam: we support per-key and per-route quotas and can map your tenant ID to Redwood metadata. Many customers implement a proxy that mints per-tenant tokens.
10:44 Aisha: questions from product: do you support function/tool calling for structured outputs? We're using actions that trigger internal workflows.
10:54 Maya: yes, we support structured outputs and function/tool calling — you can define tool schemas and Redwood will surface them. We'll attach the API examples.
11:07 Priya: can we run a small benchmark — say 2k generated requests with our prompt set and measure p50/p95 on hosted vs dedicated?
11:16 Maya: yes — that's exactly what we suggest. Please share prompt set and traffic histogram. We'll run benchmarks and include caching/batching config.
11:27 Tom: timeline? We can get sample prompts ready by Monday.
11:31 Aisha: yes, we can get that to you.
11:34 Maya: great — next steps recap — I'll send pricing + security pack; Liam will send LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and the proxy pattern; Aisha will send prompts and traffic profile; we'll schedule an SE deep dive to scope the pilot.
11:49 Aisha: thanks, sounds good.
11:51 Maya: Cool — thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with links to the repos and docs.
12:00 Call ends.

Notes: Transcript has some minor transcription artifacts (product names occasionally mis-transcribed). References shared: Redwood SE repo (link to be provided), security pack (link), pricing spreadsheet (link).
